title: Well, the Redeemer's Gone
description: Well, the Redeemer's Gone in Tonic Solfa to FRANCONIA, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 7 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 36, headed “Christ's intercession”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to FRANCONIA; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Well, the Re-deem-er's gone T'ap-pear be-fore our God, To sprin-kle o'er the fla-ming throne With his a-ton-ing blood.

lines: To sprinkle o'er the flaming throne
If justice call for sinners' blood,
The Father lays his thunder by,
And looks, and smiles, and loves.
Jesus the priest receives our songs,
And bears them to the King.
But, Lord how weak are mortal strains
Are all the notes we sing!
Sweet Saviour, tune our songs anew,
And they shall please the King.

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to FRANCONIA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
